x: Leo Lyons

A good turn out in spite of the snow and ice resulting in Simon Williamson taking his first Club Championship medal, with good runs from Leo Lyons and Tony Binda emphasising their continuing improvement in performance.
While Leo Lyons and Tony Binda show positive improvements with each outing. Results: 1.P.Rowland (Horsham B.S.) 38.16; 2.P.Magner (Epsom & E.) 38.31; 3.D.Cowles (Westbury) 38.42;
Congratulations also to Liz and Leo Lyons on the safe arrival on March 22nd of their first baby - a daughter, Amanda who weighed in at 6lb 10oz.

Of course it has been good to note the steady improvements of Leo Lyons; Tony Binda; Mick Gleave and Simon Williamson, as well as the exploits of some of our Juniors as recorded elsewhere in these pages, but in the main all these efforts have been in the form of individual achievements.
Leo Lyons won his first track championship beating Laurie and Tony Binda in an intriguing race. Leo took the lead from the start and proceeded to run the opposition into the ground.

Laurie again proved better than the opposition and won from Tony Binda and Leo Lyons. 1.L.O'Hara 15.49; 2.A.Binda 15.52; 3.L.Lyons 16.04; 4.T.Dorset 16.14; 5.M.Head 16.22; 6.A.Fairclough 16.24; 7.L.Coy 16.25; 8.D.Downey 16.52; 9.N.Kirmatzis 17.10; 10.J.Rayner 17.18; 11.M.Lake 17.19; 12.A.Grant 17.20…

- The consistant runs of Simon Williamson & Leo Lyons until injury struck Leo. - The emerging talents of Adam Christie & Mike Nouch and not forgetting Mark Sinclair's first (of many we hope) Club Senior C.C. title.

Ann has presented John Rayner with their first son Jack, while Liz and Leo Lyons are counting their blessings because their second daughter, who was due in December, arrived 12weeks premature in September.
At West London Stadium on November 7th Richard O'Hara, Francis Ward and Leo Lyons all ran p.b.'s in the 3000m. Richard finished 2nd in 9.00.1, Francis 3rd in 9.02.4 and Leo 8th in 9.09.1.
Leo Lyons showed a return to form after prolonged injury while 15 year old Gary McGurren ran an exceptional 16.16 in his first attempt at this event.

As it was Chris Millbank continued his rapid improvement with Derek Clack and Mike Donoghue gaining well deserved medals. Leo Lyons was disappointed with his time but had been unable to train due to 'flu.
Leo Lyons and Martin Lake confirmed their rapid improvement leading Belgrave to double team victories with excellent p.b's in what is regarded as one of the toughest 20's around.

Ken again triumphed in the discus and almost sneaked a win in the shot. Will Willson, Dave Catling, Leo Lyons and Nigel Clarke competing in the BAL for the first time, all performed exceptionally well.

A fine first championship for Martin Lake with Leo Lyons confirming his steady improvement. 1.M.Lake 59.39; 2.L.Lyons 60.51; 3.Mike Lake * 61.22; 4.M.Bizio 62.49; 5.M.Nouch 63.32; 6.D.Jardine 65.38; 7.D.Clack 66.56; 8.A.Painter 66.56; 9.D.Slann 67.07; 10.J.Riach 67.11; 11.N.Kidd 68.36; 12.L.Mclean 6…
Martin Lake too ran brilliantly on a reported 30 miles a week training schedule. Leo Lyons missed the start! But pride of place went again to Oliver Foote.

Leo Lyons had a great run, to ensure Belgrave continued their fine success in this event by taking the Bronze. Results: 1.I.Lamplough (Boxhill) 28.53; 2.M.Bliss (Basingstoke) 29.04; 3.N.Hilder (AFD) 29.16.

Championship, 2nd in a Cross Country race at Haywards Heath and well placed in the Southern Vets in which we were also placed in the Team events. Leo Lyons in the Southern Vets Cross Country League was the individual winner. Tony Stone won the 45 group in the V.A.C.

In the over 40's Leo Lyons ran a good first leg in 20:04. Over 40: 1, Brighton & Hove 78:16; 2, Aldershot F&D 78:25; 3, Verlea 79:24; ...24, Belgrave A (L.Lyons 20:44, A.Stone 21:31, A.Painter 21:34, R.Pearson 20:37); 53, Belgrave B 90:56 (R.Bale 21:28, D.Maughan 23:01, B.Webster 22:40, L.Coy 23:47).
Wins came from Charlie Dickinson and Leo Lyons in the M40 age group 5,000 metres and 3,000 metres steeplechase respectively. The times were good too - 15:38.4 and 10:29.6.
Also, with John Bicourt unavailable most weekends and injuries to Pete Gilby, Leo Lyons and Charlie Dickinson it was another case of what it might have been.

Leo Lyons ran to an excellent third place in the Championship race on June 18th after pushing the early pace. His time of 27.51 shows what good form he was in before injuring himself in a 3000m steeplechase shortly afterwards.

But Brighton and Hove, nearly a minute down had Nigel Gates who stormed round in 17:58 to come home a good 40 seconds clear. It was good to see Leo Lyons back for Belgrave after a long time off through injury. He ran very well on the first leg clocking 20:22.

We should not let this race result slip by without remarking how good it is to see that Leo Lyons is back on song again - not a bad time either! 1, L.Lyons 27:19; 6, A.Painter 29:43; 9, C.Taplin 31:13; 12, J.Wasbrough 31:48; 14, C.Walker 32:10; 18, L.Mann 33:09; 28, D.Maughan 37:05.
